title: Next.js: Cache poisoning of shared fallback shells in Cache Components via request-supplied placeholder route params…
description: Next.js versions 16.4.0 through 16.4.4, when self-hosted with cacheComponents enabled and partialPrefetching disabled, are vulnerable to cache poisoning of shared fallback shells via request-supplied placeholder route parameters. An unauthenticated attacker can poison the fallback shell cache entry shared by a family of routes, causing persistent 404 responses or incorrect parameter rendering in server-side HTML. No script injection or data disclosure occurs. The issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.
